_note: Default agronomic parameters for the Central American Dry Corridor postrera. Values are starting points from FAO-56 and must be reviewed by a local agronomist (CENTA) before use. Stage lengths are in days: [initial, development, mid-season, late].

_sources.kc_and_stages: Allen et al. (1998), FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56, Tables 11-12, adjusted to short postrera cycles
_sources.wrsi_classes: FEWS NET Water Requirement Satisfaction Index (WRSI): >=80 good, 60-80 partial, <60 failure
_sources.crop_traits: FAO ECOCROP and CENTA crop guides (summarized, to validate)
_sources.baseline_system: Maize-bean relay ('frijol de relevo': beans sown between maize rows at maize physiological maturity) is the documented smallholder system at the El Salvador site in Eash et al. (2019), J. Agric. Sci., doi:10.1017/S0021859619000571. GEOGLAM Crop Monitor lists Primera maize and beans, Segunda maize and Postrera beans for Central America.
_sources.bean_excess_rain: GEOGLAM Crop Monitor special report (Nov 2023): Postrera beans are sensitive to excess moisture. The mm threshold is a placeholder to validate locally.

A.label: Current: relay bean after maize
A.description: The usual system: beans sown between the maize rows once the primera maize matures. Short cycle, fixes nitrogen, but sensitive to both drought and heavy late rains.

B.label: Sorghum + bean
B.description: Part of the plot goes to drought-tolerant sorghum (grain and forage), the rest to beans. Deep roots and longer ground cover protect sloped soil.

C.label: Second maize
C.description: A second maize crop instead of beans, to rebuild the grain reserve after a lost primera. Highest water demand of the three and no nitrogen return.

soil_whc_mm._note: Plant-available water in the root zone by coarse texture class (approximate).
